newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi blames U.S. for U.N. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi blames U.S. for U.N. sanctions.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi accused the U.N. Security Council of being an instrument of the United States after the council renewed sanctions on Tripoli for not complying with demands related to the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner.

"What is going on against the Great Jamahiriya is illogical and has nothing to do with the U.N. charter and international law," the official Libyan news agency JANA on Sunday quoted Gaddafi as saying.

The Security Council on Friday voted in favour of continuing the sanctions, imposed in 1992 when Libya refused to extradite to Britain or the United States two men indicted in both countries on charges of planting a bomb aboard the plane, which exploded over the Scottish village of Lockerbie killing 270 people, including 11 on the ground..
"You cannot rely on the Security Council because it is fully in the hands of America," Gaddafi told a rally in the southern Libya city of Sebha on Saturday, said Jana, monitored in Tunis.

The decision, announced by council President Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland, followed a periodic 120-day review of the sanctions, which include an air embargo, a ban on arms sales and the downgrading of diplomatic relations.
The sanctions were toughened in 1993 to include a freeze of some of Libya's assets abroad and a ban on import of certain types of equipment used in oil terminals and refineries.
Libya repeatedly said it was willing let the two suspects be tried in a neutral country. Washington and London insist the trial must be in the United States or Britain.
